data.text/markdown:
Mobile robot kinematics: differential drive vs. holonomic

This notebook uses the MRPT Python wheel (pip install mrpt3) to simulate how two kinds of mobile robots move when they receive velocity commands, and how uncertain dead reckoning (odometry) becomes over time. It uses three MRPT modules:
  • mrpt.kinematics: velocity commands (CVehicleVelCmd_DiffDriven, CVehicleVelCmd_Holo) and kinematic simulators (CVehicleSimul_DiffDriven, CVehicleSimul_Holo).
  • mrpt.obs: the probabilistic odometry motion model used by particle filters (CActionRobotMovement2D).
  • mrpt.poses and mrpt.random: SE(2) poses (CPose2D) and MRPT's random generator, seeded for repeatable results.
Move the sliders: every plot is recomputed. Try a square path with both robots to see how differently they move.

1. Differential-drive robot

A robot with two independently driven wheels (like most indoor robots and robot vacuums) is commanded with a linear speed ||(v||) and an angular speed ||(\omega||). It cannot move sideways: keeping ||((v, \omega)||) constant drives it along a circular arc of radius ||(R = v / \omega||), and ||(v = 0||) makes it spin in place. Any path is a sequence of such arcs. Below, a short program of CVehicleVelCmd_DiffDriven commands is sent to the simulator CVehicleSimul_DiffDriven with movementCommand(v, ω).

2. Odometry uncertainty

The robot above measures its motion by counting wheel turns (odometry), but real wheels slip and their radii are never exactly known, so small errors accumulate. The simulator integrates the commands perfectly (its own odometry error model is not exposed to Python), so here we take its output as the odometry readings and ask: where may the robot really be? Particle filters answer that with a probabilistic motion model. For each odometry increment (every 0.5 s), CActionRobotMovement2D.computeFromOdometry() sets up the model of Thrun et al. ("Probabilistic Robotics"), and drawSingleSample() draws a random version of the true motion. Chaining those samples gives possible true paths. Note how small heading errors grow into large lateral errors as the robot keeps moving.

data.text/html: Motion model (1σ errors)

data.text/markdown: After 20 s and 10.0 m, the true position differs from odometry by 0.46 m (median; worst sample: 1.44 m), and the heading by 7.6° (1σ).

3. Holonomic robot

An omnidirectional robot (e.g. with mecanum or omni wheels) can move in any direction regardless of its heading. CVehicleSimul_Holo models one whose commands (CVehicleVelCmd_Holo) are a speed, a direction of motion (relative to the robot heading), a ramp time during which the velocity changes smoothly from the current to the new one, and a rotation speed used to turn the robot towards the motion direction. Here a simple controller drives the robot through the corners of a 4 m square: every 0.1 s it sends a command towards the next corner. A long ramp time rounds the corners (and may overshoot them), while the rotation speed sets how fast the heading follows the motion. With zero rotation speed, the robot slides around the square always facing the same way.

data.text/markdown: The holonomic robot went around the square in 17.0 s.
